thread:
alistair: Heads up — prod continuous-batcher tok/sec dropped ~35% after the 6b1f3a merge (PR #4921). Queueing latency spiked, tails are much worse. Seeing sustained throughput loss across two Dedicated pools. :warning:

maya: Yikes. Is this after the kernel-selection heuristics change or the KV cache prefetch tweak?

alistair: Appears correlated with the new kernel fallback ordering in runtime/kernel_policy. The PR changed preferred kernels for medium-length seqs. Also some KV cache lock contention increased in the same window.

jon: eng-ci just posted a perf regression on the canary: `perf/ctb-throughput` failed at 2445006800. Logs show token/sec down ~30% vs baseline. Linking: https://ci.internal/perf/2445006800

eng-bot: [CI] perf/ctb-throughput — FAILED — regression detected (+31% latency, -29% tok/sec). See artifacts: https://ci.internal/artifacts/2445006800

maya: Any quick mitigations? If kernel fallback order is the issue we can force older policy via config and hold the rollout.

jon: I'm starting a bisect. Local command: `git bisect start 6b1f3a^ 6b1f3a -- gui-perf-harness --bench ctb`

jon: First run shows commit 6b1f3a changes kernel preference & moved copy path earlier. On my reproduce harness tok/sec drops ~28%.

sasha: Attaching a flame sample from staging (20s window) — looks like heavy time in fallback memcopy path and scheduling coalescer stall: 

```
Flame 20s:
- 34% kernel_selector::choose_fallback_copy
- 18% kvcache::get_or_lock
- 15% coalescer::wait_for_batch
- 10% runtime::memcpy_safe
- remainder user + sys
```

sasha: Also saw a spike in kvcache lock waits coincident with kernel fallback churn. Might be that moving the fallback copy earlier increases memcopy frequency causing contention and longer queue hold.

qa-bot: Reproduced on a small cluster (3x A100) with dataset X. Baseline 110k tok/s -> 75k tok/s after the change (32% drop). Tests attached.

maya: If that's true, two options: 1) revert the kernel policy change, 2) short-term config override to prefer legacy kernel for medium seqs + open follow-up to optimize fallback path. Revert is fastest to restore SLAs.

jon: I pushed a candidate override patch to config: `scheduler.kernel_preference.medium=legacy_copy`. Rolling to canary now.

eng-bot: [deploy] rollout started for config/override to canary pool at 2445007120

alistair: Canary looks better but not perfect — tok/sec recovered to ~95% of baseline on canary nodes. Still seeing kvcache lock jitter on heavier traces.

jon: Ran a quick micro-benchmark to isolate memcopy cost: switching to legacy path reduces memcopy hotspots by ~40% in our harness. So kernel choice is the dominant factor, but KV contention amplifies it.

sasha: Suggest small follow-ups: (A) tighten fallback to avoid frequent kernel swaps within same request, (B) batch memcpy into async copy path if available, (C) KV cache sharding to reduce lock granularity.

maya: For now I'm recommending holding the full rollout and applying revert if the canary stabilizes. Need engineer owner for a proper bisect PR to revert 6b1f3a.

jon: I'll open the revert PR and include the canary override as temporary config. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4987

eng-bot: [CI] perf/ctb-throughput (post-override) — PASSED on canary at 2445007380 — tok/sec within 3% of baseline.

alistair: Great. Can we add a perf CI guard to flag kernel-selection changes next time? Maybe a targeted microbenchmark in the merge pipeline.

maya: Agreed. I'll open a ticket to add perf unit for kernel_selector and a KV contention test. Also add a monitor alert for sudden tok/sec drops.

sasha: Filing follow-ups: RUNTIME-1123 (fallback dedupe), RUNTIME-1124 (async-memcopy prototype), RUNTIME-1125 (kvcache lock sharding).

alistair: Nice work. Once revert PR merges we'll monitor for 24h then proceed with a rework branch for kernel selection + KV fixes. :thumbsup:
